activities.name: Bills of Interest - Exchange of Letters

dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts Air and Marine Operations personnel of CBP conducting foreign operations and foreign individuals or entities eligible to file claims.
dimensions.evidence: Employees of U.S. Customs and Border Protection designated with the authorities granted to officers and agents of Air and Marine Operations may provide the support

dimensions.assessment: Modifies legal liabilities by permitting financial damage payouts for injury, property loss, or death arising from foreign operations.
dimensions.evidence: pay claims for money damages against the United States... which arise in a foreign country in connection with U.S. Customs and Border Protection operations

dimensions.assessment: Permits the Secretary to expend already-appropriated operating funds to pay foreign money damage claims, without authorizing new funds.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary may expend funds that have been appropriated or otherwise made available for the operating expenses of the Department to pay claims

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to create specific statutory allowances for foreign cooperative operations and claims management.
dimensions.evidence: Section 411(f) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 211(f)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Foreign operational support provisions are permanent statutory changes, while the specific claims expenditure authority sunsets after five years.
dimensions.evidence: The expenditure authority under clause (i) shall expire on the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this subparagraph.

missing_information: Estimated total monetary value or volume of expected foreign claims against the agency.
importance_detail.rationale: The legislation expands permitted foreign activities for specific CBP personnel and allows appropriated funds to pay certain foreign tort claims, introducing a five-year sunset on the claim expenditure authority.
